title: Fact
description:
A mathematical statement as a first-class object, independent of its status.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Every other resource in this repository holds either a formal statement or a status, never both. A `claim` carries prose in `statement` and a CNF *generator recipe* in `formal`, so nothing downstream can reason with what it asserts. A kernel declaration is formal but exists only once proved, and links to no concept, ledger or evidence row. A curriculum node is a topic. A math-education concept is prose with a label. So there was no object that could hold `forall a b : Nat, a + b = b + a` AND say open / conjectured / computed / proved / refuted, with its dependencies and its evidence.

WHAT IT UNLOCKS. A fact is the object the self-extension loop operates on: pick an `open` fact whose `depends_on` are all established, dispatch its `formal.statement` to the solver, reconstruct the result into the kernel, attach evidence, flip the status, record the axiom footprint. Each of those stages exists today and keeps its own incompatible record; this is the shared one.

SELF-CONTAINMENT IS A REQUIREMENT. A fact must stand alone on `formal.statement` plus `status` plus `evidence`. `concept_refs` are provenance and gloss, never substance -- so a public repository works while a source corpus stays private, and nothing needs vendoring or republishing.

RELATION TO `claim`. A claim is an *evidence row about an instance*: it says a specific value was computed and how to re-derive it. A fact is the *proposition*. Claims reference facts through `evidence[].supports`; they are not superseded by them.

id.description: Stable identifier, `F:` prefixed, e.g. `F:nat-add-comm`. Mirrors the `C:`/`TQ:` convention of the concept graph so the two can be cited side by side.

statement.description: The proposition in prose, for a human. Never the machine-readable form -- that is `formal.statement`. Kept because a formal statement alone is not reviewable.

formal.description: What is asserted, machine-readably. This is the field that distinguishes a fact from a claim: a claim's `formal` is a generator recipe, this is the proposition itself.

language.description: `smtlib2` is dispatchable to the solver; `lean4` is checkable by the kernel; `axeyum-ir` is the internal term form.

statement.description: The proposition in the named language. For `smtlib2`, an assertion whose NEGATION being unsat establishes the fact.

fragment.description: The theory that decides it, e.g. `QF_LIA`, `Nat`, `QF_NRA`, or `none` when no fragment we have decides it. Drives reachability queries.

free_symbols.description: Symbols the statement quantifies over or leaves free, so a consumer need not re-parse to know its shape.

epistemic_status.description: Deliberately the SAME vocabulary as `claim.schema.json` and the math-education concept graph, plus `refuted`. A fact can be refuted; a claim, being a record of something established, cannot.

depends_on.description: Other facts this one rests on. This is the DAG the build order comes from -- over STATEMENTS, not topics. May be empty for a foundational fact.

axiom_footprint.description: The axioms the establishing evidence rests on, e.g. [] for axiom-free or ["propext", "Classical.choice", "Quot.sound"]. REQUIRED when `epistemic_status` is `proved`: an empty array means axiom-free and is a strictly stronger claim than an absent field. This is the metric the project publishes.

evidence.description: Zero or more artifacts establishing the status. Deliberately the same shape as `claim.schema.json`'s evidence rows so one checker can walk both. A fact with `epistemic_status: open` carries an empty array -- and that is a statement, not an omission.

kind.description: `kernel-term` is a proof term an independent kernel type-checks -- the strongest. `claim-ref` points at an existing `artifacts/claims/` entry, which is how a computed value becomes evidence for a proposition.

concept_refs.description: Gloss and provenance only, NEVER substance. A fact must be intelligible without resolving these, so that a public repository works while a source corpus stays private.

established_by.description: What settled it: a lane, a solver route, an import, or a person.

source.description: Where the statement came from, if extracted rather than authored.
